newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks up in London, tech sector leads. [CORRECTED 12:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks up in London, tech sector leads. [CORRECTED 12:55 GMT]

text.p: U.S. technology shares led most other U.S. stocks higher in London on Tuesday after Intel Corp, a bellwether for the technology industry, exceeded expectations with its third quarter results.
London brokers said the Dow, which added some 40 points on Monday to close above the 6,000 level for the first time ever, could open by as much as 30 points higher.
"The market is looking good. There's a lot of interest in the technology sector after Intel's results," said one.
Shares in Intel were up $7-1/2 to $115 in London, after rising $2-1/4 in New York on Monday.
After Wall Street closed on Monday, Intel reported a 40 percent jump in third quarter profits.

Shares in Intel pulled up most other shares in its sector, even those in Texas Instruments Inc, which is expected to report little change in its third quarter profits today. Texas Instruments shares were up $1 in London to $56-3/4.
Chrysler shares climbed $1/4 in London to $33 after reporting on Monday that its third quarter profits nearly doubled. The shares advanced $1 in New York yesterday.

Shares in Ford Motor were up $3/8 to $33-1/8 in London on expectations it would also report strong third quarter results tomorrow. Shares in General Motors added $3/8 to $52-1/4 ahead of the release of its third quarter results today.

In trading on Globex, the December S&P 500 futures contract surged 3.85 points by 1044 GMT to 711.35, a new life-of-contract high. The December 30-year Treasury bond futures contract was up 6/32 at 110-26/32.
(Corrects to delete all references to General Electric)
